after_notes: Single-owner ESP-IDF UART2 firmware initialization, bounded ingress, request dispatch, AP announcements, and subscription cadence/timeout behavior are implemented with focused lifecycle and source-ownership tests plus the canonical firmware package; see docs/parity/evidence/bap001-firmware-interface/summary.md and docs/parity/work-plans/20260821T020549Z-BAP-001/WORKLOG.md. Live Ultra 205 evidence bound to one boot of exact package `ecc7f122` (boot ordinal and reset category unchanged; uptime advance within 67 ms of host time) shows the UART2 owner answering at 115200 8-N-1 on J6: `REQ systemInfo` and `REQ shares` answered, `SUB hashrate` acknowledged, updated only on change and unsubscribed; see docs/parity/evidence/20261014-bap-uart-live-probe.md. Not verified: the live `deviceModel` answer is the board version `205`, while the reference sends the family name (`DEVICE_CONFIG.family.name`, `Ultra`); subscription values for `fan_speed` (percent vs RPM), `best_difficulty` (number vs suffixed string), `voltage`/`current` (V/A vs mV/mA) and `chipTemp`/`vrTemp`/`power` formatting differ from the reference code without an accepted-behavior record (`task-parity-bap-value-sources`). Non-claims: settings and their effects, Wi-Fi password subscription, the 300-second subscription timeout, AP-mode announcements on bound firmware, accessory electrical behavior (host was a CP2102 adapter on three wires), other boards.
